objective: Prove for any orientation of a square-lattice torus: (1) for every primitive period d, exactly one of: a directed closed walk W with det([W], d) < 0, or a dual directed closed walk of class exactly d; (2) the primitive classes of directed closed walks are exactly the primitive periods of a closed convex cone C, and those of the dual are exactly the primitive periods of its polar; (3) under a twist the cone is {0}, a line or the plane, recovering the exact duality; (4) for the uniform orientation the law of C is invariant under the polar map and the torus symmetries, so on square tori P(no horizontal winding) = P(pure vertical directed cycles both ways) and P(positive horizontal winding) = 1 - P(pure horizontal directed cycle); Newman, Grassberger and Ziff's 3/4 is equivalent to P(no directed horizontal winding) = 1/4. Check by independent negative-cycle detection and bounded cover searches on small tori.
status: Proved by SC-TORUS-EXACT-20261022-001A-P001 (V1 prose proof with sampled checks on eight small untwisted and twisted tori): for any orientation of a square-lattice torus and primitive period d, exactly one of a directed closed walk with negative pairing against d or a dual directed closed walk of class d; hence directed classes are the primitive periods of a convex cone C and the dual's those of its polar (cone types {0}, ray, line, sector, half-plane, plane); under a twist C is {0}, a line or the plane. For the uniform orientation the law of C is polar-invariant, so on square tori P(no horizontal winding) = P(pure vertical cycles both ways) and P(positive horizontal winding) = 1 - P(pure (1,0) cycle) >= 1/2; the conjectured 3/4 is equivalent to P(no directed horizontal winding) = 1/4. The derivation attempt fixes the meaning of 3/4 and of half a bit but not their values.
title: Proof: the directed cone of a random orientation on a torus
